entry.hook: 盘古斧 Pangu Axe (Supreme Creation Divine Weapon) is not a weapon. It is the Law of Cosmic Division made manifest. To wield it is not to hold a tool, but to become a living axiom of destruction and genesis, a force that does not choose its target—it chooses the nature of reality itself.

body.body_1:
盘古斧 (Pangu Axe)
至高开辟神器 (Supreme Creation Divine Weapon)
Artifact Tier: Primordial Divine Armament (太古神兵)
Current Holder: None. The Axe does not exist at any fixed point in space-time.
Current Status: The Axe is not a persistent object. It exists only within the singular, irreversible moment of the primary act of cosmic creation.
Core Attribute: Law of Cosmic Division.
body.body_2: The Pangu Axe is classified as a Primordial Divine Armament, the highest and most foundational tier of artifact. Its sole, supreme power is the act of 'breaking' and 'creating'. The Axe can sever any form of existence: physical matter, energy, space, time, cause and effect, cosmic law, and even the undifferentiated substance of Chaos itself. Each swing of the Pangu Axe marks the end of one 'boundary' and the beginning of another. Theoretically, the Axe possesses the ultimate power to terminate or restart the entire universe. There is no known upper limit to its power, as its function is absolute rather than quantitative. No minimum cultivation realm is recorded for wielding it, as the prerequisite is not a level of power but a qualification of metaphysical identity.
body.body_3: The Pangu Axe was not 'refined' or 'forged' from any pre-existing material. It was not assembled from heavenly materials or earthly treasures. The Axe was spontaneously condensed from the 'Intent of Creation' (开辟意志) borne by Pangu himself at the moment the Dao entrusted him with the mission of cosmic division. As such, its 'material' is not a physical substance but a metaphysical principle: the pure, undiluted Law of Creation-Severing. There is no record of any natural resource being extracted or any geographical region being destroyed to form it, precisely because its creation was an act of cosmic law, not an act of forging. The Axe's origin leaves no scar upon the world because it predates the world itself.
body.body_4: The Pangu Axe possesses no Qi Ling (器灵), no imprisoned soul, and no conscious will of its own. It is not a sentient entity. Its 'animation' is not driven by a captive spirit but by the pure, self-executing principle of 'Opening'. The Axe does not hunger, does not hate, and does not desire. It simply is. Its power is an extension of the Law it embodies, and its actions are the inevitable, impersonal operations of that Law. This makes it paradoxically more absolute and more dangerous than any artifact with a soul. An artifact with a will can be reasoned with, tempted, or deceived. The Pangu Axe cannot, because there is no 'with' to negotiate.
body.body_5: The relationship between the Pangu Axe and its wielder is unlike any master-recognition ritual. There is no blood pact, no oath, no soul-binding. The sole 'condition' for wielding the Axe is that the wielder must be its legitimate heir by metaphysical lineage—someone who carries the true Qualifying Bloodline of Pangu and possesses the Mandate to sever reality. Anyone else who attempts to grasp its handle would find it immovable, as if it were welded into the very fabric of existence. The Axe does not 'devour' its master, because it has no will to assert. However, the sheer purity of its 'Creation-Severing' power will erase any 'impurity' it contacts. A wielder who is not the absolute embodiment of the Dao's creative intent would themselves be treated as 'old impurities' and be annihilated by the Axe's power the moment they attempted to swing it. This is not a betrayal; it is physics.
body.body_6: The Pangu Axe has only one recorded wielder in all of cosmic history: Pangu himself. He used it for a single, world-defining act: to split the primordial Chaos and separate the clear Yang (清阳) from the turbid Yin (浊阴), thereby creating Heaven and Earth. After this single, climactic use, the Axe did not pass to a successor. It did not fall into another's hands. It disappeared from the continuum of space and time, returning to the metaphysical 'moment' of creation. No other figure is recorded as having held it. No 'previous owners' exist to be cataloged. The Axe's history is the history of Pangu's single swing, and nothing more.
body.body_7: The Pangu Axe was fully activated only once: the moment Pangu struck the primordial Chaos, cleaving the undivided cosmic egg into clarity and substance. This single swing permanently established the framework of the Tian Di Gang Chang (天地纲常), the fundamental order of yin and yang, and the dimensional structure of the Three Realms. There is no record of the Axe having a 'usage limit' or a 'time limit', because it was only used once before its nature changed. The Axe's power was not 'depleted' by this act; it was consumed into the very order it created. After this one use, it ceased to exist as an independent object, having spent its entire being to make the stable cosmos possible.
body.body_8: The Pangu Axe has no paired or complementary artifact. Its power is singular, complete, and non-dual. No artifact is known to specifically counter it, as it operates on a principle (the severing of reality itself) that precedes all other artifacts and laws. However, it is considered the ultimate ancestor of all later divine weapons and treasures. Every future sword, axe, or spear that carries the power of 'severing' or 'breaking' draws, in a metaphysical sense, upon the precedent established by the Pangu Axe. It is the archetype from which all other 'cutting' laws are derived. The Axe is also the closest surviving echo of Pangu's own body and will, making it the single most direct link to the act of creation itself.
body.body_9: The Pangu Axe does not currently exist in any identifiable location within the Three Realms or any Grotto-Heaven. It is not hidden, sealed, sleeping, or held. It is, strictly speaking, a non-localized phenomenon. The Axe exists only as a potential, latent within the fabric of reality that it created. To 'obtain' the Pangu Axe would not be to find it in a cave or a treasury; it would require being able to steal the 'moment of creation' from the memory of the universe. No entity in the known mythos is recorded as having attempted or succeeded in such a feat.
body.body_10: None. No physical ruins, stone inscriptions, or surviving scriptures are known to record the forging or use of the Pangu Axe. The only 'record' of its existence is the stable, ordered universe itself, which is the permanent scar of its single, world-forming swing.
body.body_11: The Pangu Axe stands as the central reference point for understanding the cosmic structure of the entire mythic framework. Its action of splitting chaos is the prerequisite for all subsequent events, from the separation of Yin and Yang (阴阳) to the solidification of the Tian Di Gang Chang (天地纲常). It defines the threshold between the primordial, undifferentiated state and the structured cosmos of the Three Realms (三界). Pangu's act of creation, using this Axe, is also the source of the Xian Tian Yi Qi (先天一炁) and the divine topography that the first innate gods would inherit. The Axe's non-existence as a persistent object is itself a key piece of lore, explaining why it cannot be used or claimed in any later era of the mythic timeline.

guide.guide_1: You know that feeling when you look at a history book and realize that one event changed everything? That's this axe. Except this axe didn't change a battle, a dynasty, or a world. It changed the non-existence of all those things into their existence. The Pangu Axe isn't a sword you sharpen or a club you swing. It's the answer to the question, 'How do you make a universe out of nothing?' The short answer is: you don't. You take a primordial nightmare of endless chaos, and you hit it with something that isn't violent—it's *decisive*. That something is this axe. It's the single most consequential tool in the entire pantheon, and it's also the one thing you will never, ever get to touch.
guide.guide_2: If you've read any Chinese mythology or played a game set in the Chinese fantasy world, you've probably seen the Pangu Axe mentioned as the ultimate secret weapon, the game-breaker, the final boss drop. In pop culture, it's often treated as the oldest and most powerful artifact in existence—which is technically true, but it misses the point entirely. The Pangu Axe is not 'a mythical weapon you can find.' It's not a piece of equipment that some future hero can pull from a stone. Its existence is tied to a single, unrepeatable act of cosmic birth. To treat it as a prize waiting to be claimed is like trying to mine the hammer that built the forge. So let's be clear from the start: this is not a weapon you can own. This is the fossilized imprint of a moment when the universe blinked.
guide.guide_3: Here's where the Pangu Axe breaks every rule of artifact lore. Most of the treasures in this volume were made: materials were ripped from the earth, souls were hammered into screaming cores, and someone paid a terrible price. But the Pangu Axe was never 'made.' It was not forged in a furnace, not blessed in a temple, not constructed by a master smith. It *condensed*. It solidified from the sheer will of Pangu as he accepted the mandate of the Dao to bring order to chaos. The 'material' of this axe is the Intent of Creation itself—a law, not a lump of metal. This means there were no rivers drained, no mountains collapsed, and no souls sacrificed to create it. The cost was not paid in blood; it was the cost of Pangu's entire being, which he gave to become the stage of the cosmos. It's the one artifact in the collection that has a clean conscience, and it's also the one that requires the least ethical negotiation.
guide.guide_4: Now, about the soul of this thing. Most artifacts that are this powerful get their 'life' by having a screaming, tormented spirit locked inside them. That's the standard horror story. The Pangu Axe doesn't have one. It has no Qi Ling (器灵) and no captive consciousness. And that makes it far more terrifying, not less. An artifact with a soul can be out-thought, tricked, or appealed to. You can negotiate with desperation. But the Pangu Axe is an execution of pure law. It doesn't care about your family, your destiny, or your noble cause. It doesn't *hate* you. It just follows its nature, which is to cut anything—including you—if you are standing in the way of a new reality. The Axe's power is not driven by anger; it is driven by logic. And logic, as anyone who has faced a perfect system knows, is the hardest thing to argue with.
guide.guide_5: This is where things get really interesting. Most great weapons have a master-recognition ritual: you bleed on them, you give them your soul, and they become yours or you become theirs. The Pangu Axe does not have a ritual. You cannot 'bind' it to yourself. The only way to wield it is to *be* the one who is supposed to wield it. And the only person in the entire history of the cosmos who qualified was Pangu. The condition is not strength, not cultivation, not wisdom—it's metaphysical identity. You must be the direct inheritor of Pangu's creation mandate, and you must be as pure a vessel of the Dao's intent as he was. If you are not that, you will not be able to lift the handle. And if you somehow did and tried to swing it, the axe would not devour you in a fit of rage. It would simply erase you as an 'impurity' in its path. There is no betrayal, no last-minute negotiation. It's just a law of physics, and you were the wrong kind of matter.
guide.guide_6: If you're looking for a list of famous wielders and their dramatic downfalls, you're going to be disappointed. The Pangu Axe has exactly one wielder: Pangu. No one else. No successor, no thief, no accidental finder. This is a one-man weapon, and that one man ceased to exist after using it. Pangu's story is not one of a king who conquered with a magic axe; it is a story of a being who held the universe's most dangerous tool for one single swing, and then gave his life—his entire body, his eyes, his breath, his marrow—to become the world that swing created. He is not a wielder who was slain by his weapon. He is a wielder who *was* his weapon for a moment, and then became everything else. If you think of it that way, he is the only wielder who ever got a happy ending, because his death was the birth of everything.
guide.guide_7: So here we are, at the end of this entry. The Pangu Axe is a weapon that cannot be held, a treasure that cannot be owned, and a tool that was used exactly once. It represents the purest version of a truth that runs through the entire volume: every artifact is a container for a cost. The cost of the Pangu Axe was not a sacrifice of blood, a crime against a river, or a soul trapped in a furnace. The cost was Pangu's own existence. He didn't pay a part of himself to swing the axe; he paid *everything*. And in doing so, he created the framework—the Tian Di Gang Chang, the Yin and Yang, the Three Realms—that makes all other artifacts possible. Every other weapon in this volume is a footnote to his single swing. That is the weight of this object: it is not a weapon you can point at an enemy. It is the signature of the universe on its own birth certificate. And you cannot hold a signature.

lore_entries.description: The Supreme Creation Divine Weapon that condensed from Pangu's own Intent of Creation (开辟意志) to split primordial Chaos into Heaven and Earth. It is not an object but a self-executing Law of Cosmic Division.

lore_entries.surface_form: Kai Pi Zhi Qi (开辟之器)
lore_entries.description: The 'Artifact of Opening and Cleaving'; a name for the Pangu Axe that emphasizes its nature as a tool for severing the undifferentiated state of Chaos.
Pure Yang; the light, rising, active portion of reality that was separated from Chaos by the Pangu Axe and became the substance of the Heavens.
Turbid Yin; the heavy, sinking, passive portion of reality that was separated and became the substance of the Earth.

faq_entries.question: Is the Pangu Axe a weapon?
faq_entries.answer: Not in any ordinary sense. It is a one-time instrument of cosmic law, not a tool for combat. It was used once to create the universe and then ceased to exist as a separate object.

faq_entries.question: Can anyone wield the Pangu Axe?
faq_entries.answer: Theoretically, only a being who is the direct metaphysical heir of Pangu with the Mandate to sever reality could lift it. In practice, no such being has ever been recorded.

faq_entries.question: Does the Pangu Axe have a trapped soul inside it?
faq_entries.answer: No. It has no Qi Ling (器灵) or captive consciousness. Its power comes from the pure, impersonal Law of Creation-Severing.

faq_entries.question: Where is the Pangu Axe now?
faq_entries.answer: It does not exist in any physical location. It has been consumed into the fabric of the reality it created, existing only as a potential within the 'moment' of creation.
